Yeah… yes, I think so. I mean, looking back, it wasn’t just something that started with this job or with adult responsibilities. I remember being like this even in grade school.

========== OUTPUT [patient] ==========
I’m not sure, honestly. I don’t think of myself as someone who’s constantly bouncing around or unable to sit in a chair, if that’s what you mean.

I mean, I probably shift around some, like crossing and uncrossing my legs or adjusting how I’m sitting, but I don’t know if that’s more than normal. If I’m waiting somewhere or I’m in a long conversation, I might get uncomfortable or kind of want to be done, but I wouldn’t say I’ve really noticed this as a major problem.

So… I guess my answer is I’m not sure. Trouble focusing, yes, I notice that more clearly. But feeling physically restless or like I can’t sit still — I don’t have a strong example of that.

I mean, looking back, it wasn’t just something that started with this job or with adult responsibilities. I remember being like this even in grade school.\n\nTeachers would say I was smart — like, “She understands the work,” that kind of thing — but then I’d lose the paper I was supposed to turn in, or I’d only do part of what the directions said because I missed some piece of it. I’d have worksheets shoved in my desk or backpack and then not be able to find them. And I needed reminders to finish classwork, not because I couldn’t do it, but because I’d kind of drift off from what I was supposed to be completing and then the time would be gone.\n\nSo, yeah, it feels familiar. The job makes it more obvious now because there are consequences and people waiting on me, but that pattern of losing track and needing reminders… that goes way back.\n\nDoctor: Do you have the same kind of forgetting and losing track of things in your life outside of work, too?\n\nPatient: Yeah… I mean, I guess the biggest thing is still work, because that’s where it’s getting me in real trouble. That’s what brought me in — I keep forgetting scheduled callbacks, work orders, and even basic follow-ups I promised people I’d do. Like I’ll tell someone, “Yeah, I’ll check on that and get back to you,” and I really do mean it in the moment, but then it just slips away.\n\nAnd now it’s not just one little mistake here or there. It’s piled up enough that work actually sent me here, which is embarrassing to say. I’m trying to move up, and I feel like I’m putting that at risk because people are starting to see me as not following through.\n\nOutside of work… I mean, I’m sure there are little examples, but the work stuff is the clearest and the most upsetting because there are people waiting on me and there are consequences. That’s where it’s become impossible to ignore.\n\nDoctor: Outside of work, do these same problems with forgetting and not following through cause trouble in your home life or relationships?\n\nPatient: Um… I’m honestly not sure how much, if that makes sense. I don’t want to say no, because I’m sure there are things at home where I forget something or don’t follow through right away, but I also don’t have a clear example jumping out at me the way the work stuff does.\n\nLike at work, it’s very obvious because there’s a work order, or a callback, or someone waiting, and then it reflects badly on me. At home it’s more… I don’t know, it blends into regular life more, maybe? I might forget something and then just deal with it later, or it’s not as formal, so nobody’s writing it down or getting on me about it in the same way.\n\nIn relationships, I guess I’d have to think about that more. I haven’t really had someone sit me down and say, “This is a major problem,” at least not in the way work has. So I don’t want to overstate it. The thing I know for sure is that work is where it’s causing the most trouble and where people are actually upset with me about it.\n\nDoctor: At home, do you also often forget things you said you would do?\n\nPatient: At home… I mean, yes, I do forget things I said I’d do, but the part that’s really gotten bad enough to bring me in is more with work. That’s where it’s not just, like, “Oh, I forgot to pick something up,” and then I fix it later. It’s scheduled callbacks, work orders, and basic follow-ups I told people I would handle.\n\nI’ll tell someone, “I’ll call you back,” or “I’ll check that work order,” or “I’ll get back to you on that,” and in the moment I fully mean it. I’m not blowing them off. But then it just… disappears from my head, or I lose track of it in everything else, and by the time I realize, it’s already late or someone else is asking why it wasn’t done.\n\nAnd it’s piled up so much that work actually sent me here, which is honestly really embarrassing. I’m trying to move up, and now I feel like I could lose that chance because people are seeing me as someone who doesn’t follow through. So yes, I can forget things outside of work too, but the clearest, most serious version of it is these work things I promised I’d do and then didn’t keep track of.\n\nDoctor: Do you often feel anxious or worried?\n\nPatient: I don’t know… I mean, I worry about the work situation because it’s become a real problem, but I’m not sure if I’d say I’m anxious or worried “often” in the way you mean.\n\nLike, if something is going wrong or I know I dropped the ball, then yeah, I’ll think about it and feel stressed about it. But I don’t know if I’m walking around anxious all the time, if that’s what you’re asking. I guess I’d need you to clarify a little what you mean by anxious — like nervous for no reason, or just worried because there are actual consequences happening?\n\nDoctor: In social situations with friends or family, do you also tend to lose track of conversations or forget plans you made?\n\nPatient: With friends or family… I’m not sure I can give you as clean an answer there. I probably do sometimes, but the place I really notice that “losing the thread” thing is when my supervisor is talking directly to me.\n\nLike, he’ll be standing right there explaining something about a repair or an audit, and I’m looking at him. I’m not looking away, I’m not trying to be rude, I’m not ignoring him. I’ll even feel like I’m listening. But then only the first part really sticks, and after that it’s like the rest doesn’t fully land. Then I have to ask him to say it again, and I hate doing that because it makes me look like I wasn’t paying attention.\n\nSo in social situations, I don’t have a strong example of forgetting plans with friends or family right now. But conversations where someone is giving me information straight to my face — yes, that happens, especially at work with my supervisor.\n\nDoctor: In your day-to-day life outside of work, do you often have trouble staying focused when someone is talking to you?\n\nPatient: Outside of work, I’m trying to think… I don’t have as clear of an example. I’m sure there are times someone at home is talking and I’m not taking it all in, but the situation I can really point to is at work, when my supervisor is talking straight to me.\n\nLike he’ll be explaining something about a repair or an audit, and I’m standing there looking right at him. I’m not on my phone, I’m not turned away, I’m not trying to ignore him. In my head I feel like I’m listening. But then what happens is the first part sticks, and after that it’s like the rest just doesn’t settle in. Then I’m left realizing I didn’t actually hold onto what he said, so I have to ask him to repeat it.\n\nThat’s the part that bothers me, because from the outside it probably looks like I just wasn’t paying attention, but I really am trying to listen. It’s more like I lose the thread even while he’s talking directly to me.\n\nDoctor: Have you been feeling down or depressed مؤخراً?\n\nPatient: I’m not really sure how to answer that. I wouldn’t immediately say I’ve been depressed, exactly. I mean, I’ve been stressed and frustrated, especially when things aren’t going well, but I don’t know if that’s the same as feeling “down or depressed.”\n\nLike, if I mess something up or I feel like I’m not keeping up, then yeah, I can feel pretty bad about myself for a while. But I don’t know that I’ve been walking around feeling sad all the time, if that’s what you mean. I guess I’d need to know what you’re counting as depressed — like feeling hopeless and low most days, or just being worn out and upset because life has been difficult lately.\n\nDoctor: When someone at home is talking to you, do you often realize afterward that you missed part of what they said?\n\nPatient: At home… I’m trying to think of a clear example, and I don’t want to just say yes if I’m not sure. I probably do miss things sometimes, but the one that really stands out to me is still at work.\n\nWhen my supervisor is talking straight to me about a repair or an audit, I’ll be looking right at him like I’m following along. I’m not trying to tune him out or anything. But then only the first part really sticks, and after that it’s like the rest kind of slips past me. Then I realize I didn’t actually get all of what he said, and I have to ask him to say it again.\n\nSo with someone at home, I can’t give you a strong “this happens all the time” answer. Like if there’s another noise nearby, or I’m already thinking about the next job I need to get to, suddenly I realize my eyes were on the words but I don’t actually know what I just read.\n\nThen I have to go back and reread the same part, sometimes more than once, just to figure out what the notes actually said. Yes. That one, yeah… that happens a lot. More than I like to admit, honestly.

I’ll put something down for what feels like two seconds — my keys, the tablet at work, a flashlight, or a tool I was literally just using — and then it’s like it disappears. I’ll be standing there thinking, okay, I just had this in my hand, I walked over here, I set it down somewhere, and then I can’t picture where. So then I’m retracing every step, checking the same bench or cart or shelf more than once, looking under papers, looking in places that don’t even make sense.

At work it’s embarrassing because it can actually hold things up. Like if I need the tablet to check something or I need the one tool I just had, the job kind of stops while I’m hunting around for it. And I know how it looks — like I’m being careless or not keeping track of my stuff — but in the moment I really did not mean to lose it. I just set it down and my brain didn’t… record where it went, I guess.

It’s especially frustrating when it’s something obvious, like the flashlight is sitting right on a ledge or the keys are in a pocket I already checked, and I’ve spent all this time getting irritated and feeling stupid over it. It’s constant enough that I kind of expect it now, but it still slows me down.
